I don't know what it is, something wrong with me. May be my thinking
is not good these days. I tried what I learnt in lite course in the
forex tester 3, EURUSD, none of them worked. :( Almost all the levels
just broke without any PA, may be I have marked them incorrectly. I
should try them later again.

Anyway I am back to my old homework with FLs. Every chart becomes a mess
 with these mouth FL and Apex FLs concepts now. Appreciate anyone's
opinion on the following diagram about marking the FLs. This is GBPUSD.

Things to note here are,

1. FL1 is created by breaking the local SR(Low) to the left

2. FL2 is created after breaking the FL1

3. FL3 is just marked because, to me, it seems it is a n obvious FL. Price has ranged below that FL (FL3)

4. FL4 is created after breaking the FL3.

But according to the IF and Harry, FL should break something to the left
 and should show some kind of a slowness in the momentum. Also from the
Markepedia, price ranges below or above FL. Obviously FL1 breaks a low,
but after that FL1 kink, price has the momentum. I cannot see a slowness
 after the FL1 kink. So in my opinion this is not a important FL. I
marked FL3 just because it looks like a great FL. it has the end of
momentum, but no good level broken to the left. In my MT4, the history
data is missing. I actually checked in fxtop. there is a good level at
1.3010. So it does break the a level also. So FL3 satisfies all the
characteristics of a FL. hence FL4 is also a valid FL. Price didn't
actually respect FL2 which is created after breaking FL1. It went back
to FL4 meaning FL4 is more important than FL2. So why FL3 and FL4 are
more important than FL1 and FL2?

FL1 just broke a local SR and FL3 broke a HTF historical low

I am gonna download the missing historic data and find more FLs like this.

author: HCDE
text:
Hi ViTaLDRuG,

Regarding USDCAD failed trade, you're right, your engulf reached a target (RS kink) comming from a line you can draw at 1.32126.

There is something that always make me very suspicious about that kind of setup.

If you draw two horizontal lines, the upper one at 1.32851 and the lower
 one at 1.32630, you can see that price breaks very very clear lows. In
that kind of configuration, retailers sell, IT's buy. If they make a
large buy position there, you can be sure that they need to break your
fake QM highs to generate buyers and swap their position from BUY to
SELL.

Hope it makes sense,

Have a good day

Hi IF,

I marked a D1 chart of the same. The FLs are different.In D1 chart the
FLF is engulfed and it is a clear PA that price wants to go lower. Price
 retraced to the source (it is not clear in the D1 chart BTW) then
drops. I actually marked the whole candle as the FL as It is not
possible to pinpoint the exact FL in D1 chart. This leads me to ask
several other questions :)

1. So In Daliy chart below, the LFL is engulfed but price hit a BSZ
level. So do we still consider it as an engulf? I mean does that engulf
is signal to go lower? I believe that it should not hit a target level
in the same TF, like in QM LL/HH case.

2. So lets say I am going to trade in H1, which was my old post above.
Then FL1 is created after breaking a local SR. But FL3 is created by
breaking a very old monthly low which is in 1986.. something. So In that
 case, FL3 is the most important right?

3. I agree IF, FL2 respected the price price, but only once. See FL3 has
 respected many times, I mean many bounces from FL3. Does that also
implies that FL3 is important?

4. Lets say I am going to trade from FL4. Then below is a possible QM
setup (two images). In last image, So FL-X is marked as my LFL (There is
 a pole going up from FL-X. it shows that momentum is not reduced. In
that case I doubt it is a FL). LFL is broken and FL-Y, the UFL is
created. Now HH has broken the FL-Y(Engulf). So it says price wants to
go up. Now this UFL is created by breaking the FL-X. All the horizontal
dotted blue lines are reactions to this FL-X. But there is another blue
rectangle, a kink which can be a FTR created by breaking all these blue
horizontal lines which are reactions to the FL-X. If we consider that
Blue rectangle for engulf, the HH is not valid for a QM, because it has
not engulfed the Blue rectangle. So my real question is, Do we consider
the highs and lows which are reactions to a FL when we check for the
validity of a QM? Is it not enough if we find the FL to which these
highs and lows are reactions to (FL-X in my case), and see if HH/LL
engulf the Approach FL (FL-Y in my case) created by breaking the FL-X?

HTF

LTF

Again, I am sorry about too many questions
